brief: Compare Cedar and Flint to choose a prompt tool for a team that needs no-login use and no server retention. Use these criteria: cost, login requirement, prompt storage, and source access. Use only the supplied fixture documents; do not browse.
criteria: Cost; login requirement; prompt storage; source access
source:
Fixture A: Cedar product documentation. Cedar composes prompts locally in the browser. It requires no login. It does not send or save prompt text on a server. Users copy prompts into another AI. It cannot fetch URLs. The document does not state a price.
Fixture B: Flint product documentation. Flint requires an account. Its paid plan costs USD 8 per month. It sends prompt text to a model API and stores saved prompts on a server. The document does not say whether unsaved prompts are retained. It can fetch public web pages. Its landing page says “10x better answers” but provides no test results.

brief: Review the retry worker for duplicate-charge risk after a timeout. Explain the failure and a targeted verification step. Use only the supplied code and API contract; do not browse.
Explain this study for an engineer deciding whether the intervention is ready to adopt. Preserve the uncertainty. Use only the supplied abstract; do not browse.
source: Fictional study abstract: Forty volunteers were randomly assigned to a short diagram lesson or a text lesson, 20 per group. The immediate assessment contained 10 questions. The diagram group averaged 7.0 correct answers and the text group averaged 6.5. The estimated difference was 0.5 points with a 95% confidence interval of [-0.3, 1.3]. There was no delayed test. The study used one lesson and one convenience sample. No data on completion time were collected.
